neighbours.label: Opening sentence of a scientific abstract in the passive: the auxiliary after a long technical subject ('A novel X method for Y ⟦is⟧ presented/proposed'); first-person or everyday sentences are quiet
fire: Abstract: A novel spectral method for the solution of nonlinear wave equations on unstructured grids is presented.
A new adaptive mesh algorithm for simulating shallow water flow over irregular terrain is proposed.
Abstract: An efficient iterative solver for large sparse linear systems arising in structural analysis is described.
A novel semi-implicit scheme for the numerical modelling of stratified atmospheric flows is presented.
Abstract: A fast multipole technique for computing electromagnetic scattering from rough surfaces is introduced.
A new perfectly matched layer formulation for elastic wave propagation in anisotropic media is proposed.
Abstract: A high-order discontinuous Galerkin method for compressible turbulent flows is developed.
A novel boundary treatment for lattice Boltzmann simulations of porous materials is presented.
quiet: In this paper, we present a spectral method for nonlinear wave equations on unstructured grids.
We wanted a faster way to simulate shallow water over rough ground, so we wrote our own code.
Our group spent two years building a solver for the large systems that engineers deal with.
The weather over the mountains is hard to predict in early spring.
My colleague is very good at computing things quickly in her head.
The old stone bridge over the river is closed for repairs.
We tried a new recipe for lentil soup last night and it is delicious.
The tall man in the grey coat is my neighbour.

notes: Card: copulas and sentence-final periods after long technical subjects in abstracts. Probes: 'Abstract: A novel finite-element scheme ... is presented' 1.04, 'A new ... numerical method is proposed' 0.39; 'was examined' 0.15, 'In this paper, we propose' 0.12, 'The aim of this study was' 0.05, everyday copulas 0.00-0.02.
